title: Unjust Decrees
summary: The passage condemns those who issue unjust decrees, deny justice to the needy and poor, and prey upon widows and the fatherless.

explicit_facts.text: Some decree unrighteous decrees and write grievousness.
They turn the needy from judgment, deny the poor their rights, and make widows their prey and rob the fatherless.

unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the people addressed and the setting are not specified.

narration.text: Wo unto them that decree unrighteous decrees

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage speaks in prophetic condemnation; the actions are not narrated as a specific witnessed event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific court, victim, or act of robbery as a narrated event.

title: The Day of Visitation
summary: The passage asks what the condemned will do in the day of visitation and desolation, and says they will bow under prisoners and fall under the slain without the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The passage asks where the condemned will flee for help and where they will leave their glory in the day of visitation and desolation.
Without the Lord, they shall bow down under prisoners and fall under the slain; the anger remains and the Lord's hand is still stretched out.

unspecified_visual_details: The day of visitation and the described prisoners and slain are not identified as a specific visible event.

narration.text: to whom will ye flee for help?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Questions and prophetic warnings; do not stage as a specific battle or present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent visible prisoners, casualties, or a battle scene.

title: Assyria as a Rod
summary: The Lord calls Assyria the rod of his anger and says he will send him against a hypocritical nation to take spoil and prey and tread the people down.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord addresses Assyria as the rod of his anger.
The Lord says he will send Assyria against a hypocritical nation to take spoil and prey and tread the people down.

unspecified_visual_details: No visible appearance of the Lord, Assyria, or the people is specified.

narration.text: O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rod and treading language is figurative prophetic teaching, not a literal supernatural scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent an Assyrian army's appearance or specific attack.

title: The Assyrian's Intent
summary: The passage says Assyria does not intend merely what the Lord intends, but seeks to destroy many nations; it recounts his boast about princes and conquered places.

explicit_facts.text: Assyria does not mean what the Lord means, but intends to destroy many nations.
Assyria says his princes are altogether kings.
Assyria compares Calno with Carchemish, Hamath with Arpad, and Samaria with Damascus.

unspecified_visual_details: The named cities are mentioned in speech and are not described as visible settings.

narration.text: in his heart it is to destroy and cut off nations not a few.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Assyrian's boasts are reported speech, not an explicitly staged present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Assyria speaking or depict the cities as a single location.

title: A Threat Against Jerusalem
summary: The passage reports Assyria's claim to have founded kingdoms of idols and his question about doing to Jerusalem what he did to Samaria.

explicit_facts.text: Assyria claims his hand founded kingdoms of idols, whose graven images excelled those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
Assyria asks whether he will do to Jerusalem and its idols as he did to Samaria and its idols.

unspecified_visual_details: No appearance of the idols, Jerusalem, or Samaria is described.

narration.text: Shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and to her idols?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is reported boasting and a rhetorical question, not a narrated attack.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict destruction of either city as occurring in this scene.

title: Punishment of Assyria
summary: After the Lord's work upon Mount Zion and Jerusalem, the king of Assyria will be punished for his pride; the passage reports his boast of strength, wisdom, conquest, and gathering riches.

explicit_facts.text: After the Lord performs his work upon Mount Zion and Jerusalem, he will punish the proud heart and high looks of the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria says that by his strength and wisdom he moved borders, robbed treasures, and put down inhabitants.
He compares gathering the riches of the people to finding a nest and gathering eggs; none moved, opened the mouth, or peeped.

unspecified_visual_details: No specific appearance, conquest, or setting is described.

narration.text: I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The nest and eggs are figures of speech. The king's claims are reported, not presented as a newly occurring scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict nest-gathering or conquered inhabitants as literal events.

title: The Instrument and Its Maker
summary: The passage compares Assyria to an ax, saw, rod, or staff that cannot boast against the one using it, then foretells the Lord's judgment.

explicit_facts.text: The passage asks whether an ax can boast against its hewer, a saw against its user, or a rod or staff lift itself against those who use it.
The Lord of Hosts will send leanness among Assyria's fat ones and kindle a burning under his glory.

unspecified_visual_details: No people or literal tools are described as visible.

narration.text: Shall the ax boast itself against him that heweth therewith?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The tool comparisons are metaphors, not literal supernatural actions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a self-moving ax, saw, rod, or staff.

title: Fire and a Reduced Forest
summary: The passage describes Israel's light and Holy One as fire and flame that consume thorns, briers, forest, and fruitful field; few trees remain.

explicit_facts.text: Israel's light will be a fire and his Holy One a flame, devouring thorns and briers in one day.
The glory of the forest and fruitful field will be consumed; they will be as when a standard-bearer faints.
Few trees of the forest will remain, few enough for a child to write them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A diminished forest and field may be represented as imagery of the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and any literal visible fire are not specified.

narration.text: And the light of Israel shall be for a fire

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage uses prophetic imagery; it does not narrate a witnessed burning.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine figure or assert a literal visible flame beyond the text's imagery.

title: The Remnant Returns
summary: The remnant of Israel and Jacob will no longer rely on the one who smote them but will rely truly on the Holy One of Israel; a remnant will return amid the decreed consumption.

explicit_facts.text: The remnant of Israel and those escaped of the house of Jacob will no longer rely on the one who smote them, but on the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
The remnant of Jacob shall return to the mighty God.
Though Israel is as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall return; the decreed consumption will overflow with righteousness.
The Lord God of Hosts will make a determined consumption in all the land.

unspecified_visual_details: No return journey, people, or landscape is specifically depicted.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic declarations, not a narrated migration scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible gathering, route, or destination.

title: A Word to Zion
summary: The Lord tells the people dwelling in Zion not to fear Assyria's rod and staff; the indignation will cease, a scourge will be stirred against Assyria, and the burden and yoke will be removed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord tells the people dwelling in Zion not to fear the Assyrian, who will smite them with a rod and lift his staff against them after the manner of Egypt.
The indignation will cease after a little while, and the Lord's anger will be in their destruction.
The Lord of Hosts will stir up a scourge for Assyria according to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb; his rod will be lifted as it was upon the sea, after the manner of Egypt.
The burden will be taken from the shoulder and the yoke from the neck; the yoke will be destroyed because of the anointing.

unspecified_visual_details: The people of Zion and the referenced past events are not described visually.

narration.text: O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Rod, scourge, and yoke are prophetic figures; references to Egypt and Midian do not make those past events present scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly, or stage the past events at the sea or at Oreb.

title: The Assyrian Advance
summary: The passage tracks Assyria's movement through Aiath, Migron, and Michmash, then across the passage to lodge at Geba; Ramath is afraid and Gibeah of Saul has fled.

explicit_facts.text: He comes to Aiath, passes to Migron, and lays up his carriages at Michmash.
They cross the passage and lodge at Geba; Ramath is afraid and Gibeah of Saul has fled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sequence indicates movement through the named places.
unspecified_visual_details: The people included in “he” and “they,” the appearance of the places, and the carriages are not specified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a narrated movement through successive locations; do not collapse all locations into one.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named individuals or give the carriages or travelers unspecified traits.

title: Calls and Flight
summary: The passage calls to the daughter of Gallim to raise her voice toward Laish and Anathoth; Madmenah is removed and the inhabitants of Gebim gather to flee.

explicit_facts.text: The daughter of Gallim is addressed and told to raise her voice so it is heard unto Laish; Anathoth is addressed as poor.
Madmenah is removed, and the inhabitants of Gebim gather to flee.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities of the addressed figures and what “Madmenah is removed” means visually are unspecified.

narration.text: Lift up the voice, O daughter of Gallim

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage does not establish that the daughter of Gallim is literally a visible person.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a speaker, a specific flight, or an interpretation of Madmenah's removal.

title: At Nob
summary: The passage says he will remain at Nob that day and shake his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

explicit_facts.text: He will remain at Nob that day and shake his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of “he,” the gesture's visibility, and the setting's appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: As yet shall he remain at Nob that day

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a gesture toward Jerusalem, not an attack on it.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jerusalem being attacked or invent the person's identity.

title: The Haughty Humbled
summary: The Lord of Hosts will lop the bough with terror, bring down the tall and humble the haughty; the thickets will be cut down with iron and Lebanon will fall by a mighty one.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord of Hosts will lop the bough with terror; the tall will be hewn down and the haughty humbled.
He will cut down forest thickets with iron, and Lebanon will fall by a mighty one.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The forest imagery may be visualized as trees being cut down.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the mighty one, and whether the bough and forest language is literal or figurative, are not specified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage closes with prophetic imagery of judgment and humbling.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible divine figure or identify the mighty one.
